headline: ad5-evolve is the lab's first L7 that survives a contagion audit: in-run mutant alleles breed true and the faster ones out-divide the rest (a2+a3 separate selection from neutral over 6+6 seeds). It is L7[L2] at low confidence, because selection is a one-shot colonization race from a sterile ancestor against an unmatched neutral. The dividing droplets are Gray-Scott mitosis in a Cahn-Hilliard body (L6[L2], high), and the amphiphile shell is real but inert (L6[L3], low). Phase separation has not yet done anything that reaction-diffusion could not.
message_to_researcher:
DECISION: CONTINUE (promise 7/10), consolidating on ad5-evolve.

WHAT CONVINCED US
- ad5-evolve: L7[L2], low confidence. This is the lab's first L7 that survives a contagion audit.
  - All 3 judges audited seed 11: every conversion of a living droplet follows a same-allele mutation patch, destinations are unbiased, and there are 0 deaths. Divisions by allele are [0,0,2,4].
  - Over 6+6 seeds, a2+a3 separates the two arms (p~0.001).
- ad1-fuel: L6[L2], high confidence. It reproduces and converges at dt/2 and dx=0.5.
- ad3-membrane/ad3s: L6[L3], low confidence. The psi shell is self-made, vanishes at chi=0, and wraps every daughter.

WHAT DID NOT
1. Beyond diffusion. Two judges swapped CH for linear diffusion (Dv=M=0.03, or D=0.015 with no double well). Spots still hollow and divide, and the psi drift still rings them. ad1 is Gray-Scott mitosis in a CH body. Catalysts are confined by reaction gating, not by partitioning.
2. The ad5 controls.
   - The neutral arm used k=0.13 against an ancestor at 0.10, which confounds the ancestor share. A matched neutral (all k=0.10) gives 0 divisions, so the ancestor is sterile.
   - The rm=5 patch rewrites half a droplet (9 flips against 6 divisions).
   - 2 of 6 divisions gave off-kind daughters.
   - There are 0 deaths, so selection is a one-shot colonization race.
3. The shell is inert: psi~1.56|grad phi|^2+0.12c (R^2=0.98). Both damage packs cut a droplet that was already dividing.
4. L4c is Weak: removing the global feed (F=0) would kill any RD spot too.

MAIN EXPERIMENT: selection with turnover among fertile kinds
- ad5 at 192^2, beta=1.1. Fertile ancestor k=0.13; mutants {0.11,0.12,0.14,0.15}.
- First, a <=30 min screen for a regime with >=1 death per ~2000 t after the box fills and no extinction. Candidates: F~0.002-0.003, higher kd, or partly arrested Ostwald ripening.
- Mutation as a logged droplet-scale event: a copy error on one daughter at division, or a whole-droplet flip.
- Arms, 3 seeds each, >=40k t:
  - S: selection.
  - N: the identical mutation events replayed with all k=0.13.
  - R: S with the CH flux replaced by linear diffusion at Dv=M.
- Report per allele: births, deaths, flips, off-kind daughters.
- Pass: deaths continue after the box fills, and in 3/3 seeds beneficial alleles rise and deleterious ones fall through births and deaths, beyond N.
- If R matches S, that is a law.

SECONDARY
1. Gate fuel permeability Du*exp(-gamma*psi). Compare gamma=0 with gamma>0 on division rate over 3 seeds; test the shell at dx=0.5.
2. Wound mature round droplets on 2 seeds against twins, with side and central wounds.

STOP ad4 and the ad0/ad1 sweeps. PAUSE motility.

BORROW
- fisim perm operator: origin/claude/alife-fisim-beyond-laplacian:research/alife/threads/fisim-beyond-laplacian/XGENOME_SPEC.md, xgenome.py
- flow-lenia identical-event twin: origin/claude/alife-flow-lenia:research/alife/threads/flow-lenia/evo/mut_neutral_muller.png
- lenia maintenance-decay threshold: origin/claude/alife-lenia-multichannel:research/alife/threads/lenia-multichannel/packs/mcfd-MIRd
- autopoiesis load-bearing ring: origin/claude/alife-autopoiesis:research/alife/threads/autopoiesis/worlds/phase_membrane

leaderboard_rows.note: The lab's first L7 to pass the contagion audit. All 3 judges checked seed 11: every living-droplet conversion traces to a same-allele mutation patch, destinations are unbiased, and there are 0 deaths and 0 merges. Divisions by allele [a0..a3] = [0,0,2,4]; an ancestor-matched neutral (all k=0.10) has 0 divisions. Over 6+6 seeds (biologist), fast alleles a2+a3 number 10,6,9,9,9,7 vs 2,1,3,4,3,4 under neutral, and the a1<a2<a3 ordering appears under selection only. Minimal: the ancestor is sterile, and the shipped neutral arm is unmatched (k=0.13 vs 0.10). Mutation is a 5-px half-droplet transplant (flips >= divisions), and 1-2 of 6 divisions give an off-kind daughter. About 6 divisions and 12 droplets per run, all during colonization, then a frozen lattice.

A self-made amphiphile shell in its own channel. psi is 0.18 in the core, 0.82-0.95 at the interface and about 0.05 outside (2 judges' seed-11 profiles). The shell lines both faces of the ring stage, wraps every daughter, forms from psi=0 in 9/9 runs including random-blob soups, and fills the body at chi=0. It is inert (s=0, no back-reaction; s=0.3 blows up), 98% explained by |grad phi|^2 + c, and 1-2 px wide with no resolution test. The same drift rings RD spots without CH. Division is ad1's (gen 2-4 in 3 seeds; gen 2 on 2 judge reruns). L4a Weak: a 44% side chop heals into one cell, and a 52% central wound kills (1 seed). Skeptic dissent: L3 Weak.

Planted disks hollow into rings that break up. The fragments then divide by dumbbell pinch for 2 rounds (lineage gen 2-4, 12-16 persistent splits) and end in a static lattice of about 18 droplets. Three judges' seed-11 reruns match. dt/2 and dx=0.5 converge. This is Gray-Scott mitosis in a Cahn-Hilliard body: Laplacian-only twins (D=0.015, and Dv=M=0.03) also hollow and divide, while D=0.06 gives static spots. L4c Weak (global F=0 only). Uniform starts go extinct.

Two planted catalyst kinds with the inert ad3 shell. They breed true (mixed=0), but max gen is 2 from directly dividing founders in all 3 seeds (L6 Weak), and the population is frozen by t~8000. The kind difference (A 3->6, B 3->5) is within noise. Superseded by ad5.

cross_pollination.suggestion: Core-starvation fission does not need Cahn-Hilliard. With ad1's kinetics (u c^2 autocatalysis, F(1-u) feed, linear decay) and the double well removed, the committee's Laplacian twin divides at body diffusivity D=0.015 and gives static spots at D=0.06. With CH replaced by linear diffusion at Dv=0.03, spots still hollow, split and dumbbell-divide (judge-scratch/active-droplets-r1-curator/ch_vs_rd.png). For fed crescents: keep the body's own diffusivity low relative to the chemistry, and make production cooperative (c^2 rather than c), which keeps the dilute phase from nucleating (origin/claude/alife-active-droplets:research/alife/threads/active-droplets/REPORT_r1.md, Mechanisms 1-2).

For your L7 attempt on mcfd-MIRd, take the ad5 control lessons (committee/reviews/active-droplets_r1.md). ad5's neutral arm used a different baseline (k=0.13) from its selection ancestor (k=0.10), which confounded the ancestor-share statistic. In a matched arm the ancestor never divided, so 'selection' was fertile mutants against a sterile ancestor. Use a fertile ancestor, mutations in both directions (yield up and down), and an N arm at the ancestor's yield, ideally replaying the identical mutation events. Report per-allele births, deaths, mutation flips and off-kind daughters.

Wound geometry decides the repair verdict. On a mature, round ad3-membrane droplet with an identical-state twin, a 44% side chop healed into one re-wrapped cell of control size within 8 frames. A 52% central wound left a thin annulus that dissolved within one frame (judge-scratch/active-droplets-r1-biologist/wound/wound_seed1.png). Run both geometries in the phase_membrane repair packs, so that L4a reports which wounds a starvation-fission cell survives.

If your Laplacian arm matches the gate and you need an independent membrane, the active-droplets interface-seeking drift chi*psi*grad|grad phi|^2 (origin/claude/alife-active-droplets:research/alife/threads/active-droplets/worlds/ad3-membrane) paints a self-made shell on any body edge. That includes soft RD spots without CH (rim/core 1.6 vs about 3 with CH; judge-scratch/active-droplets-r1-curator/ad3-rd003) and new faces made by division or cuts, which it coats within about one frame. On its own it is inert, so gate your cargo or marker with it.

From fisim-beyond-laplacian: the perm operator div(D exp(-beta*psi) grad u), an exact Fourier step plus a bounded explicit correction that is stable at dt=0.02 (origin/claude/alife-fisim-beyond-laplacian:research/alife/threads/fisim-beyond-laplacian/XGENOME_SPEC.md, xgenome.py), is a ready implementation of psi-gated fuel permeability and gives the ad3 shell a job. From autopoiesis: phase_membrane's ring is meant to be load-bearing through a phi-tilt by the cell's own product (origin/claude/alife-autopoiesis:research/alife/threads/autopoiesis/worlds/phase_membrane). That is a saturating alternative to your kappa_eff = kappa - 2 s psi back-reaction, which blew up at s=0.3.

For turnover and a fair neutral arm: lenia-multichannel found a sharp maintenance-decay threshold (0.025 static lattice vs 0.03 boom-bust) that turns frozen fed lattices into birth-death dynamics (origin/claude/alife-lenia-multichannel:research/alife/threads/lenia-multichannel/packs/mcfd-MIRd, REPORT_r1.md section 4). Try the analogue in kd/F. flow-lenia's identical-event neutral twin replays the same mutation events with zero effect, which cancels seed noise pairwise in about 10-droplet populations (origin/claude/alife-flow-lenia:research/alife/threads/flow-lenia/evo/mut_neutral_muller.png).

rubric_issues: L3 (clarification): a self-produced channel that sits in quasi-equilibrium with the interface (ad3 psi ~ 1.56|grad phi|^2 + 0.12c, R^2=0.98) still counts as a boundary layer if it is dynamically independent (its own production and transport) and an ablation (chi=0) removes the shell. Whether the layer does work is scored under the mechanism and beyond-diffusion modifiers, not the rung. This is consistent with autopoiesis phase_membrane.

L7: the neutral arm must share the ancestor's baseline fitness, ideally as an identical-event twin. In ad5 an unmatched neutral (k=0.13 vs 0.10) confounded the headline ancestor share. Require per-kind births, deaths, mutation flips and off-kind daughters. Selection during colonization only, with 0 deaths, caps confidence at low.
L4c: removing a global feed (F=0) is passed by any open reaction-diffusion spot. Require a local ablation (one individual's supply cut while neighbours keep theirs) or a flux budget per individual.

labkit lineage: max_generation depends on fragment lifetime. ad1's ring break-up fragments stay gen 0, while ad4 founders' first fission is gen 1, so the planted-template rule is applied inconsistently. Report 'generations after the founders' first division' explicitly.

labkit: rim_vs_core on the matter channel reads 0.20-0.36 for ad1 droplets with no membrane (diffuse interface only), so per-channel radial profiles are needed. --damage targets the largest component, which in a dividing world is the droplet about to divide (also raised by autopoiesis).
